podcast.title: Missed Gig Due to Calendar Error (1991)
podcast.body: In late November 1991, Jerry Cantrell went hunting, having promised to return for an important Alice in Chains gig on December 1st. He mistakenly believed that November had 31 days, leading him to miss the scheduled show. Upon his return on December 2nd (which he thought was December 1st), he was surprised to discover he had missed the performance. As a Christmas gift that year, his record label presented him with his very own pocket calendar. "Jerry honestly believed that November has 31 days and he ended up missing the gig."

podcast.title: The Cable Guy Soundtrack Contribution (1996)
podcast.body: Jerry Cantrell of Alice in Chains contributed to *The Cable Guy* soundtrack in 1996, an album associated with the "creepy Jim Carrey vehicle" film. The soundtrack also featured other artists like Silverchair, Porno for Pyros, and Cracker. "Silver Chair Jerry Cantrell of Allyson Chains, Porno for Pyrrho's Cracker, and primitive radio gods ended up with a hit with standing outside a broken phone booth with money in my hand."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Installation of Home Recording Outfit for Layne Staley (Post-1997)
podcast.body: Jerry Cantrell, the guitarist for Alice in Chains, installed a home recording outfit in Layne Staley's condo. This was done after Staley moved into the condo in April 1997, providing him with the means to record music at home, although Staley only used it occasionally. "Allison Chains guitarist Jerry Cantrell installed a home recording outfit that Lane used once in a while, but mostly he just painted, watched TV, played video games, and did drugs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Decent but Lesser Solo Work
podcast.body: Jerry Cantrell has released "some decent solo records," but none have achieved the same level of impact or success as the collective accomplishments of Alice in Chains. "And a lot of some decent solo records, but nothing anywhere near the order of what Allyson accomplished together."

xref.title: Condo Purchase and Isolation (April 1997)
xref.body: In April 1997, Layne Staley moved into a three-bedroom, 1500 square foot condo in Seattle's University District, purchased for $262,000 by the LaRusta Trust, part of the Alice in Chains Management Company. Staley used "John LaRusta" as an alias to keep his real name out of public records. He spent his time painting, watching TV, playing video games, and doing "lots and lots of drugs." Alice in Chains guitarist Jerry Cantrell installed a home recording outfit for him, which Staley used only occasionally, further highlighting his increasing isolation. "The purchaser was the LaRusta Trust, which was part of the Allison Chains Management Company. John LaRusta was an alias used by Lane. He did one his real name used in any public records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Breakup Activities (1997-2002)
xref.body: After Alice in Chains broke up in November 1997 due to Layne Staley's inactivity, guitarist Jerry Cantrell installed a home recording outfit in Layne's condo. However, Layne rarely used it, spending most of his time painting, watching TV, playing video games, and consuming "lots and lots of drugs." "With nothing happening with their frontman, Allison Chains broke up in November 1997."

xref.title: Recording Outfit for Layne Staley (Post-1997)
xref.body: Alice in Chains guitarist Jerry Cantrell installed a home recording outfit in Layne Staley's condo. This was an effort to allow Staley to continue making music, although he reportedly used it only "once in a while," preferring to paint, watch TV, play video games, and do drugs. "Allison Chains guitarist Jerry Cantrell installed a home recording outfit that Lane used once in a while, but mostly he just painted, watched TV, played video games, and did drugs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Layne Staley Found Dead April 19, 2002; William DuVall Joined, Three Albums Followed
xref.body: Layne Staley was the person around whom Alice in Chains was originally formed in 1984. By 1995, heroin had rendered him almost unable to function; the band could neither record nor tour. His body was found on April 19, 2002, in his Seattle condo after two weeks of no contact, still with a syringe in its arm. After a 2004 tsunami benefit with various substitute vocalists, the band decided to continue and eventually settled on William DuVall from a Los Angeles band called Comes with the Fall — who could blend his voice with guitarist Jerry Cantrell's harmonics and was also a capable guitarist. Three Alice in Chains albums followed. "He was also a pretty fair guitar player."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Indian Ocean Tsunami Benefit Catalyst (Boxing Day 2004)
xref.body: The reunion process began when Jerry Cantrell, Mike Inez, and Sean Kinney were asked to perform at a benefit concert for victims of the Indian Ocean tsunami, agreeing to play with a series of guest singers. "The thing that started the reunion was the Indian Ocean tsunami on Boxing Day 2004."

xref.title: Formation and Name Origin
xref.body: Layne Staley had been living with a homeless Jerry Cantrell at their rehearsal space when Sleeze, Staley's band, was eventually renamed Alice in Chains. After Staley's other band (a funk outfit) and Cantrell's separate project both broke up, Cantrell and Sean Kinney asked Staley to be the vocalist for their new group, adopting the name of Staley's former band, Alice in Chains, for the new project. "Sleeze was eventually renamed Alice in Chains, while Lane was living with a homeless Jerry Cantrell at their rehearsal space."

xref.title: Founding Members and Early Lineup
xref.body: Guitarist Jerry Cantrell and drummer Sean Kinney were the founders of Alice in Chains. Layne Staley was not a founder; he was drafted in early from a glam band called Sleeze, for whom he played drums. "That was guitarist Jerry Cantrell and drummer Sean Kinney. But he was drafted in early from another band, a glam group called Sleeze, for whom he played drums."

xref.title: Jerry Cantrell Collaboration
xref.body: The band opened for one of Jerry Cantrell's solo tours around 2002 and also served as his backing band on that tour, fostering a friendship that led to William DuVall joining Alice in Chains. "Later, the band opened for one of Cantrell solo tours. This would be about 2002. In fact, Come With The Fall also function as Jerry's backing band on that solo tour."

xref.title: Layne Staley's Vocal Style
xref.body: Layne Staley's voice and his harmonies with Jerry Cantrell were central to the band's sound, considered the best hard rock harmonies since David Lee Roth and Michael Anthony in Van Halen's early days. Their vocal arrangements often featured dual lead vocals, strategically overlapped, with the two voices typically separated by a major third. Staley, with the more powerful delivery, could transition from a menacing monotone to sharp, cutting explosions, and also had a great scream, appealing to both metal and alternative fans. "Technically, the two voices were separated by a major third with Lane having the more powerful of the two deliveries."

xref.title: William DuVall Joins as Singer
xref.body: William DuVall, then singer for the Atlanta band Come With The Fall, had met Jerry Cantrell around 2000, and his band later opened for and functioned as Cantrell's backing band on solo tours around 2002. Their developing friendship led to DuVall becoming the new permanent singer for Alice in Chains. "Everybody became friends, talked to him to having DuVall be a permanent new singer for Alison Chains. And it happened."
